Subject: Profiling results & fallback strategy for cost/perf tuning

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for the session last week. I pulled together the profiling artifacts from our sandbox runs and sketched a suggested fallback and routing policy so your integration stays within the latency targets while we iterate on model choices. Attachments: brightgrid-profiling-20261019.csv, kvcache-sample.txt, quant-profiles.pdf.

High-level summary:
- Baseline (gpt-small-ish) average p95 latency at your 512-token median request was ~210ms; cost headroom looks thin for 100k qps-equivalent bursts.
- KV cache hits on session prefixes drove a ~35% token-cost reduction in the sample trace (see kvcache-sample.txt).
- Quant profile q8_az reduced GPU memory footprint but increased CPU post-processing time — recommend trying q4_0 for long-running streams where latency matters.

Recommended immediate plan (implementation handoff items):
1) Short-term: enable prefix KV caching (auto-ttl 24h) + conservative batching (max_batch_delay=10ms, max_batch_tokens=4096). This should lower per-token cost without violating p95.
2) Medium-term: enable model-variant routing: primary=redwood/gpt-x-small (q4_0), fallback=redwood/gpt-x-tiny (q8_az) when queue depth > 15 or instance health signals degrade.
3) Quant selection: start with q4_0 for production routes; add q8_az on a canary route for cost-sensitive background jobs.
4) Observability: add a per-route token-cost and p95 alert (thresholds: p95 > 350ms or token_cost delta > 15% week-over-week).

Ask: Can your infra team enable sample traffic to the staging endpoint tomorrow morning (10/21) 09:00 PT? We will run an A/B: current config vs. caching + q4_0.

I'll hand this off to Monica and Dylan for implementation details — Monica will own routing policy config and Dylan will own quant/batching changes.

Thanks,
Hannah

Quick answers:
1) TTL: 24h was conservative based on the sample; we can make it session-aware (sliding TTL) for your multi-hour sessions so we don't evict active prefixes prematurely. We'll wire a metric for "kv_cache_miss_rate_by_session_len" so we can tune after two days of sampling.
2) Routing: Redwood supports policy-driven routing natively — you can specify routing conditions by queue depth, instance health, or a cost/latency score. No external proxy required. We'll send the policy snippet in the next message.

- Dylan to deploy q4_0 build to the staging pool (canary fraction 10%).
